request_mark_hint: Select text in the URL or Body and click <0>{{marker}}</0> to mark it as a payload position. Header values can be marked the same way.
attack_desc_sniper: One payload set. Each payload is tried in each position in turn, one at a time; other positions keep their original value. Good for fuzzing one parameter at a time.
attack_desc_battering_ram: One payload set. The same payload is placed into every position at once. Good for testing a repeated value (e.g. the same token in two places).
attack_desc_pitchfork: One payload set per position, all advancing together. Total requests = the shortest set's length. Good for pairing related values (e.g. username + matching password).
attack_desc_cluster_bomb: One payload set per position, trying every combination. Total requests = the product of all set lengths. Good for brute-forcing unrelated fields together.
speed_hint_fast: Fast: {{concurrency}} concurrent requests, {{timeout}}s timeout. Quickest, but more likely to trip account lockouts, rate limits, or overload the target.
speed_hint_normal: Normal: {{concurrency}} concurrent requests, {{timeout}}s timeout. Balanced default.
speed_hint_cautious: Cautious: {{concurrency}} concurrent requests, {{timeout}}s timeout. Gentler on lockout-prone logins and rate-limited targets.
rate_limit_hint: Throttled to at most {{rate}}/s regardless of concurrency, spacing requests out with a delay between dispatches.
no_positions_marked: No positions marked yet; mark at least one value above to configure payloads.
start_error_no_position: Mark at least one payload position with §…§ first.
guide_intro: Burp Intruder's idea: mark spots in a request, throw payloads at them, and compare every response.
guide_step1_body: Select some text in the URL or Body and click <0>§</0>: it wraps the selection in <1>§…§</1> markers. Header values can be marked the same way. Each marked spot becomes one position, numbered in the order they appear (URL, then headers, then body).
guide_step2_body: <0>Sniper</0> tests one position at a time with a single payload set. <1>Battering ram</1> puts the same payload in every position at once. <2>Pitchfork</2> pairs up one payload set per position, advancing together (e.g. matching username + password lists). <3>Cluster bomb</3> tries every combination across one payload set per position: the most thorough, and the most requests.
guide_step3_body: Each position needing a set gets its own panel with three sources: <0>Simple list</0> (paste values, one per line), <1>Common passwords</1> (the built-in wordlist of 1000 real leaked/common passwords, click "Preview" to browse it before using it), or <2>Number range</2> (from/to/step, with optional zero-padding).
guide_step4_body: Type a string you expect to see only in a successful response (e.g. <0>Welcome back</0>). Any result containing it gets flagged with a checkmark in the Match column, so you can spot the hit in a sea of 403s at a glance.
guide_step5_title: Click "Start attack" and watch the table fill in
guide_step5_body: Results stream in live as each request completes. Click a column header to sort by status, length or time; click a row to see the exact request that was sent and the full response it got back. "Stop" cancels a running attack at any point.
guide_footer_note: This fires real requests at the target, one per payload combination (up to 20,000 per attack). Only use it against hosts you're authorized to test.
